clauses.reason: The order revokes Executive Order No. 9544 of April 25, 1945, which authorized the Secretary of War to assume full control of the public airport on the described Oregon lands, and states that the lands are included in a twenty-year lease to the City of Redmond from March 12, 1942 and that it is intended that "the lease shall again be operative and" (the sentence continues on a later page). The order says the earlier order "is hereby revoked" and states no later effective date, so the revocation took effect when the order was signed, March 22, 1948, and was exhausted by performance on that date.

The closing words state that the lease is to be operative "in full force and effect upon the signing" of the order. The reactivation is tied to the signing of the order, March 22, 1948, so the statement was performed on that date and nothing in it remained to be done afterwards.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 9938 (13 FR 1555, Federal Register of March 24, 1948; PDF pages 1-3 of the held machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF) is headed Oregon, Revoking Executive Order No. 9544 of April 25, 1945, Authorizing the Secretary of War to Assume Control of a Certain Airport. Identity: number, subject and date agree with the census register row (1948-03-22). The held text prints the order in pieces. The order begins on PDF page 1 and breaks at "the lease shall again be operative and" with the note that it continues on page 1557. The closing words are printed on PDF page 3 as "in full force and effect upon the signing" followed by "of this order." and the signature of Harry S. Truman, and the line "March 22, 1948." with the Federal Register filing line (FR Doc. 48-2642, filed March 22, 1948, 4:26 p.m.) is printed further on PDF page 3 after unrelated table-of-contents matter, which is how the page layout scrambled the page. The American Presidency Project mirror text of the order agrees with the Federal Register pieces, joins them into one sentence and gives March 22, 1948; the Federal Register text is the registered source and is the one quoted here. Inventory (corrected from the dossier's single clause, which ran across unrelated table-of-contents and other documents): two clauses, each a contiguous span of the held text. The first (characters 3421 to 4233) is the authority recital, the revocation of Executive Order No. 9544 of April 25, 1945 as to the described Oregon airport lands (1,520 acres), and the statement that the lands are included in a twenty-year lease to the City of Redmond from March 12, 1942, beginning the intention that the lease again be operative. The second (characters 13002 to 13060) is the closing of that sentence, "in full force and effect upon the signing" of the order. Ending: the revocation says Executive Order No. 9544 "is hereby revoked" and the closing words tie the lease's reactivation to "the signing of this order"; neither has a deferred effective date, so both were performed on signing, March 22, 1948 (the date printed in the held Federal Register text, which agrees with the filing date), and each clause is exhausted by performance on that date. The machine own-term candidate of 1962-03-12 is the end of the Redmond lease described in the order; it is a fact about the lease, not an end of the order's revocation, so it is not used. Searches: a by-number search of the held order texts for EO 9938 returns 0 matches, so no held later order cites it; the Federal Register disposition-note, U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit naming this order. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 9544 stays revoked and the lease operates again; that consequence is not a command left to end. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning.
